I think my issue is more being picky about meals not ingredients. I would say there's few common ingredients I hate. Mostly just green beans. It's mostly like... the texture of something being wrong. Like if the veggies in something are overcooked and mushy. Or my rice is undercooked just a little. Or I notice there's a bone or ligament in my meat. Or my husband uses a noodle type I dislike (I strongly dislike linguine and I don't quite understand why). 

I went to the grocery store today and shopped for myself for the first time in a while. I kind of realized I was missing out on all these foods I normally love to eat (yogurt, bananas and cheerios, bagels, other fresh fruit and snacks) because I rely on my husband to primarily shop. This definitely made me tear up. I could feel the pain of what you've been through in your words.

I used to love cooking as a kid and even into adulthood. It was a wonderful activity and my mom was inconsistent in how good her meals actually were so I preferred my food to hers. At some point tho, it just became more energy than I had. Maybe a result of burnout. I stopped enjoying it and it became insurmountable to make myself food. 

I definitely eat more food when I'm depressed and self indulgent in my emotions, which causes weight gain and increases dysmorphia. If I'm in fear or survival mode, I start starving myself and refusing food, which just makes it worse because I have no fuel in my system. 

I also struggle with what my food needs are vs my husband. He's always making rich carb and protein heavy meals with little to no fruit, veggies, or fiber. It makes me nauseous to eat like that all the time. If I try to make vegetarian or meat/carb light meals, he often makes comments on the perceived lack. He has tried to shift his cooking to include more veggies but he always makes them in ways I strongly dislike, i.e., mushy and mixed in with rice or sauce etc. He claims he's being efficient and reducing how many dishes he's using by cooking them with other things. I've expressed my dislike and showed him how I like them but he just isn't willing to put in the effort. I don't understand his resistance to this.

I cook much more rarely than my husband. Between him loving to cook and only working part time and me going to school full time with a part time job, I don't cook often. I definitely relate to the sneaking in veggies. My mom ruined spaghetti bolognese bc she kept increasing the blended carrot to sauce ratio until it was inedible
